fieldMarks: Small, 2.5-3.9 cm; gray, green, reddish-brown, sometimes blackish or silvery white.
Black mask-like stripe through each eye, often extending along the side of the body.
Light-bordered black spots on sides and groin; yellow groin and inner thighs.
Call is a sharp metallic 'tink' or high peeps about 1-1.5 per second; breeding males have a dark throat.
behavior: Secretive and nocturnal, rarely seen outside the winter breeding season (November-March).
Burrows into the ground among roots when inactive; migrates between breeding pools and upland habitat.
Females lay 10-100 eggs in clusters attached to vegetation; eats small terrestrial invertebrates.
habitat: Sandhills, pine flatwoods and upland pine forests; breeds in small fishless wetlands such as Carolina bays, flooded meadows, ditches and cypress ponds.
range: Coastal Plain of the southeastern United States, absent from southern peninsular Florida. Not in Canada.
